subject: MAP: Technical evaluation plan — post-call recap
message_1_subject: MAP: Technical evaluation plan — post-call recap
message_1_body:
Thanks for the time today — great discussion. Putting a short post-call recap and suggested MAP milestone for the technical evaluation so we have a working draft to iterate on.

Key takeaways from today:
- Goal: validate model selection and serving configuration for Acme's customer-facing summarization pipeline (use-case: customer support ticket summarization + extraction).
- Success signals: match quality on Acme's internal eval set, latency and cost targets (see below), and absence of PII leakage in outputs.
- Acme will provide a representative sample of 1,000 anonymized tickets + evaluation labels and an ops contact (Priya) for perf runs.

Proposed MAP milestone: Technical evaluation plan (draft):
1) Milestone: Benchmark & model shortlist (owner: Redwood + Acme) — deliverable: filled benchmark template + summary report
   - Redwood provides: benchmark-results-template.xlsx, recommended model shortlist and runtime/quantization suggestions
   - Acme provides: anonymized eval set, evaluation labels, acceptance criteria
   - Target completion: 2026-03-10
2) Milestone: Performance validation (owner: Acme SRE + Redwood solutions)
   - Success criteria (suggested): p95 latency < 350ms for 256-token generate at 4 concurrent request streams AND median latency < 120ms for 64-token inference; cost objective: aim to keep inference cost under $0.50 per 1k output tokens for production config (we'll iterate).
   - Also include memory/throughput checks for dedicated vs hosted options
   - Target completion: 2026-03-12
3) Milestone: Quality sign-off (owner: Acme product + Redwood ML lead)
   - Acceptance: task-specific metrics (F1/ROUGE/Exact Match depending on evaluator) meet agreed thresholds; no high-severity regressions on safety/PII tests
   - Target completion / close: 2026-03-15 (target close for MAP milestone)

Dependencies & blockers:
- Acme to share anonymized eval dataset and the technical contact for test infra by 2026-02-24
- Access to a staging environment or temporary credentials for throughput testing (if Acme prefers on-prem testing)

Next steps (action items):
- Alex / Priya: confirm dataset share cadence and who on your SRE team will own perf runs by Tue 2/24.
- David (cc'd): I'll loop you into the benchmark template and we'll plan a 90-min kickoff to walk through the metrics and runtime knobs.
- I'll attach a MAP draft with milestone language to sign off on in the next week.

Thanks — happy to adjust targets once Priya shares constraints.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference

(415) 555-0123

message_3_subject: MAP draft (v2) + benchmark template — technical evaluation plan
message_3_body:
Per our follow-up: attached is MAP-draft-v2.pdf with the milestone language and the benchmark-results-template.xlsx for the perf/quality runs. Highlights from the draft:

Milestones (concise):
- M1 (Benchmark & shortlist) — due 2026-03-10 — Redwood: populate model configs & run baseline for 3 model families; Acme: provide dataset + acceptance criteria
- M2 (Perf validation) — due 2026-03-12 — run on Acme staging (preferred) or Redwood dedicated for parity; collect p50/p95/p99, memory and throughput metrics
- M3 (Quality sign-off & rollout plan) — due 2026-03-15 — agreed model & serving config for pilot

Responsibilities:
- Acme: provide anonymized dataset, labels, and SRE time for perf runs; confirm data transfer mechanism
- Redwood: provide benchmark template, recommended model shortlist and quantization/runtime suggestions, one 90-min kickoff session, and a final summary report with recommended production config and cost estimates

Model shortlist (initial recommendations):
- Llama 2 70B (8-bit / q4f16) — strong quality for summarization, higher mem footprint
- Mistral 7B Instruct (q4) — good quality/cost tradeoff for latency-sensitive runs
- Open weights (eval): smaller 13B family for fast iteration (cost-optimized pass)

Suggested quantitative targets (draft):
- Quality: task-specific metric (F1/ROUGE variant) to be agreed; preliminary acceptance: F1 >= 0.80 on Acme's label set or no more than 10% degradation vs current baseline
- Latency: p95 < 350ms for 256-token generation with 4 concurrent workers; median < 120ms for 64-token inference
- Cost: target <$0.50 per 1k output tokens for production-oriented config (will refine with batch/kv-cache tuning)

Attachments: MAP-draft-v2.pdf, benchmark-results-template.xlsx (please download and populate the template with one representative run).

I'll follow up to schedule the 90-min kickoff next week; propose Tue 2/25 or Wed 2/26 — Priya / Alex, which works for you?

Best,
Marissa
message_4_subject: Re: MAP draft (v2) + benchmark template — technical evaluation plan
message_4_body:
Adding a quick note from solutions / eval perspective — thanks for the draft, Marissa. A few concrete suggestions to tighten the acceptance criteria and make the bench runs actionable:

Bench success criteria (recommended):
- Quality: use a stratified sample from Acme's labels; require primary metric (e.g., ROUGE-L or task F1) >= 0.80 and no more than 5% of samples with hallucination or PII hits flagged by the safety check.
- Latency: collect p50/p95/p99 across 30-minute steady-state runs at target concurrency (4 workers). p95 target < 350ms for 256-token responses; note: dedicated GPU runs may show 20-30% better p95 vs hosted for large models.
- Cost: report cost per 1k output tokens across each model/config; include batch size and kv-cache settings. Aim for a production target <$0.50 per 1k tokens for the preferred config; call out cost/latency trade-offs deliberately in the summary report.

Model/run recommendations for the first pass:
- Pass A (quality-first): Llama 2 70B (8-bit q4f16), Redwood runtime with optimized kernels
- Pass B (cost/latency): Mistral 7B Instruct (q4) on a batching-optimized runtime; consider 13B family for a fast iterate baseline

Operational asks:
- If Acme wants us to run on Redwood dedicated capacity, we'll need requested time window (2-4 hours) and expected concurrency so we can reserve capacity.
- Please populate the benchmark sheet with one canonical run and share S3 location / access method.

I'm available for the kickoff on Wed 2/26 10:00-11:30 PT; if that works we'll send a calendar invite and agenda.

-rk
